responses.evidence: The pair now picks the revert reading and says so in both behaviors. B-07's exit-path list declares "the round writes a malformed cleaner-escalation.json ⇒ reset to the round's input checkpoint; outcome ESCALATION_MALFORMED ... its checkpoint is discarded by this reset and is therefore never gated, so ESCALATION_MALFORMED is the round's whole outcome and no PASS/REVERTED can also be recorded for it", under the heading "each path has exactly one reset target and exactly one recorded round outcome, so no discarded checkpoint is afterwards gated". B-13's malformed clause is restated to match: "it is not treated as a plain cleaner round, because B-07's malformed exit path has already git reset --hard'ed the worktree to the round's input checkpoint, so the round's checkpoint is discarded and is never gated — the earlier 'still gated' reading is withdrawn, and no second outcome (PASS, FAIL or REVERTED) is recorded for that round." The manifest's B-07 and B-13 then/observableResult carry the same single tree state and single outcome, and B-07's observable now asserts "that path's single recorded outcome, and that no gate result exists for a discarded malformed checkpoint". ESCALATION_MALFORMED, not REVERTED, is the recorded outcome so that B-14's PersistedQualityStageRound union — which is outside this finding's routed behavior scope and is unchanged — keeps every member reachable; FAIL is likewise assigned to the throw/cancel path. B-08 is untouched and no longer conflicts: it speaks only of a green regression bundle, and a malformed round has no surviving checkpoint to be "PASS at the last checkpoint".

Both behaviors now name one reset target for the escalation path, taking the finding's first option: B-07 excepts the escalation path from its input-checkpoint rule and defers to B-13's accepted-tree reset. B-07's fourth exit path reads "the round writes a valid escalation ⇒ reset to the accepted tree; outcome ESCALATED (B-13) ... this is the one documented exception to the input-checkpoint target and the two targets differ from round 2 on ... In round 1 the two targets are the same commit; from round 2 on the accepted tree is the target", with the recorded reason (the escalation returns the slice to the generator loop and invalidates the accepted tree's baseline citation, so every post-approval cleaner commit is discarded rather than only the escalating round's). B-13 states it identically: "reset to the accepted tree first — the one exception to B-07's input-checkpoint reset target, declared there and stated identically here, so an escalation raised in round 2 or 3 has one post-reset HEAD and not two". The two declared unit assertions are now one: the manifest's B-07 observable asserts "the accepted tree and not round 1's output commit for the round-2 escalation" and B-13's asserts "for the round-2 valid escalation, that HEAD is the accepted tree rather than round 1's output commit", and both test-plan bullets pin the escalation case to round 2 so the round-1 coincidence cannot hide the claim.

The contract now cites the signature, which is the finding's first clear option, so src/candidate-gate-phase.ts stays out of scope and P-04's exclusion is safe rather than hopeful. runCandidateGatePhase's declared parameters are `declarations: readonly GateDeclaration[]` and an optional `cache?: GateCacheOptions` documented in the source as "forwarded verbatim to runGates ... a pure pass-through: this phase decides nothing about reuse" (src/candidate-gate-phase.ts:47-72) — so an arbitrary declaration list and the round-0 cache options are admitted with no additive parameter. GateDeclaration.stage is typed `stage: string` and validated only as non-blank (src/gate-runner.ts:130 and the `declaration.stage.trim() === ""` refusal at :451), and the phase only copies it (`stage: GateResult["stage"]`), so the new "clean" stage string and the new suppressions declaration pass through unedited alongside the deterministic and full-suite members. That citation is written into B-04, into B-06, and into P-04 itself, and the manifest's B-04, B-06 and P-04 entries carry both the citation and `typecheck` among their gateIds so the "compiles against the unedited signature" half is observed by a gate rather than asserted in prose.
